column3: Pairs God's provision with eating and the same ban on Satan's steps.
Addresses seeking help through patience and prayer, not the food or Satan warning.
Calls for lawful, good provision and gratitude, reinforcing the food command.
Repeats the Satan-steps warning and open-enemy rationale in a wider call to surrender.
Links eating good provision with gratitude and worship.
States that Satan's steps command indecency and wrong, explaining the warning's danger.
Restates that Satan is an open enemy who can divert people.
Uses eating for the consequence of concealing revelation, not dietary guidance.
Affirms a broad baseline of permitted food before specified prohibitions.
Shows Satan causing Adam and his wife to slip, supporting his hostile role.
Concerns those killed in God's path.
Joins eating good things to righteous action for the messengers.
Forbids worshipping Satan and calls him an open enemy.

Calls all people to believe and follow the messenger for guidance.

Notes abundant fruits from which people eat.
